neighbours.label: physically hot or cold water or packs applied to or handled near the body
fire: Dip the burned finger in a bowl of icy water right away.
He filled the tub with hot water and lowered himself in slowly.
The nurse laid a cold pack on her forehead to ease the fever.
Steep the herbs in boiling water, then hold the warm cloth on your chest.
She scalded her wrist when the kettle tipped over at breakfast.
Put a hot water bottle under the blanket by his feet.
After the run, athletes sit in an ice bath for ten minutes.
Cool the child with a lukewarm sponge and remove the heavy clothes.
quiet: Dab the cut finger with a dry tissue right away.
He filled the form with his name and handed it over slowly.
The nurse laid a paper chart on her desk to read later.
Grind the herbs into a powder, then hold the cloth bag by the string.
She sprained her wrist when the ladder tipped over at breakfast.
Put a soft pillow under the blanket by his feet.
After the run, athletes stretch on a mat for ten minutes.
Calm the child with a quiet story and remove the heavy shoes.

short: hot or cold on the body
notes: Probes: 0.45-0.79 for ice, steaming, scalding, boiling, frozen; figurative 'hot new single' 0.02; 'a hot day' 0.18. Plain liquids also leak ('salt water' 0.52 at ' of'), so these near misses are non-liquid first-aid and household items. The test therefore does not separate temperature from water alone.
